release_notes.en-US: Clarifies why the store lists sensitive-data categories and separates captured Lightstreamer application data, requested MCP sharing, and usage analytics. Full payload inspection, existing data-category declarations, permissions, consent controls, and analytics defaults are retained. Supports the published MCP companion 0.1.8.

version.approval_notes: Version 2.0.10 clarifies privacy documentation and listing wording. Full payload inspection and the existing native data categories are retained. Sensitive categories can occur inside captured application values; captured Evidence is excluded from usage analytics. Inspected URLs and application location values do not require browser-history or device-location access. Desktop Firefox 140+; regular browsing only. Open Developer Tools on an application using the official Lightstreamer Web Client and choose the Lightstreamer Workbench panel. The extension observes clients, subscriptions, Item Updates and outbound Client Messages without suppressing application behavior. Local Injection is local; Server Injection uses the application's normal sendMessage path after review. The optional local MCP companion uses loopback WebSocket connections and shares captured application data under the installation data permissions; instructions are bundled and documented at https://imom39a.github.io/lightstreamer-workbench-extension/docs/agent-access/. Technical and interaction analytics require both Firefox's optional native consent and the Workbench preference. Application data is excluded from analytics. The paired source ZIP contains exact committed source, locked dependencies and reviewer build instructions, with only the publicly extractable analytics ingestion configuration. Publisher, account, signing and npm credentials are excluded. Generated React DOM innerHTML code is framework code; application-controlled values are rendered as text.
